create.title: Finite beta-mask Cauchy-Green connector identity
create.statement_tex: Let A=s-z/2=x+iy and R=[x_1,x_0] times [-T,T]. For the complete finite meromorphic transition integrand F(A;z) and a prescribed C^1 height mask Theta(y;z), positive rectangle orientation gives V_(x0)=V_(x1)+H_+-H_-+2 pi i sum_(p in R) Theta(Im p;z) Res_(A=p)F-intint_R partial_y Theta(y;z)F(x+iy;z)dxdy. For the hierarchical mask Theta_beta=psi(beta), partial_y Theta_beta=psi'(beta) and the full A=0 residue is crossed. For the disjoint mask Theta_beta=psi(beta)(1-psi(alpha)), alpha=beta+Im z, the connector has both terms psi'(beta)(1-psi(alpha))-psi(beta)psi'(alpha), and its A=0 residue is weighted by 1-psi(Im z). The residue of zeta(1-A) at A=0 is -1. All finite outside sides, profiles, floors, endpoint stars, axial/top/corner terms, and the external -(4/pi)X^(1/4) real-part normalization remain. This identity supplies no transition estimate and does not control a masked R1 share.
create.next_action: Use one explicit partition convention. Keep E1 and R1 recombined through the displacement, and do not infer a bound for a filtered R1 share from the unmasked Round-24 estimate.

create.title: Corrected beta-transition stationary character kernel
create.statement_tex: In the positive-alpha interior of the accepted beta-transition normal form, partial_alpha Psi=log(alpha D_j/(pi q sqrt(Xx))), alpha_0=pi q sqrt(Xx)/D_j, and |Psi''(alpha_0)|=alpha_0^(-1). Multiplying the Round-20 gamma power alpha^(sigma+Re(z)/2-1/2), the arithmetic factor h^(-sigma+Re(z)/2)q^(-sigma-Re(z)/2), and the stationary factor alpha_0^(1/2) leaves exactly q^0. The leading q-phase is exp(-i q theta_j(x)), theta_j(x)=pi sqrt(Xx)/D_j. For D_M^chi(theta)=sum_(q<=M)chi_4(q)exp(-iqtheta), sup_(M<=Q)|D_M^chi(theta)|<<min(Q,1+|cos theta|^(-1)) and its one-period L1 norm is <<log(2Q); interval sums carry the discrete-BV norm of their amplitude. For integral D_0 and odd q, |D_0-q/2|>=1/2. These conclusions do not supply the phase-pushforward density, complete actual-profile q-BV bound, Hilbert-pole uniformity, endpoint control, or outside-height limit needed for the transition estimate.
create.next_action: Derive the exact radial phase pushforward and an integrable uniform discrete-BV bound for the complete actual-profile amplitude, separating the hard top Hilbert pole from smooth interior scales.

update.statement_tex: Choose and record either a hierarchical beta mask psi(beta), which contains the double-bounded box, or a disjoint mask psi(beta)(1-psi(alpha)), which has two connector edges and crosses only a filtered A=0 residue share. Using the proved finite Cauchy-Green identity, displace the complete recombined radial integrand without separating the artificial E1/R1 pole. Then physicalize the shifted line plus connector and prove normalized O_epsilon(X^epsilon) using a controlled radial phase pushforward and complete-profile q-BV estimate for the q^0 period-four character kernel, uniformly through the hard top Hilbert pole, mask edges, radial endpoints, and finite outside-height limits.
update.next_action: Adopt the hierarchical partition, prove the double-bounded share and recombined E1+R1 displacement are target-safe, then establish the radial pushforward and complete-profile q-BV theorem with hard top and smooth interior scales separated.
Complete the beta radial-pushforward/BV estimate, including its full residue ledger, before returning to the alpha-bounded zeta-high branch.
Use the recombined E1+R1 displacement; do not reopen the accepted unmasked physical endpoint and R1 bounds or apply them to an isolated masked share.

reject.reason: The stationary Hessian factor alpha_0^(1/2) changes the apparent power: the exact total exponent is q^0, consistent with the exact sine kernel. The chi_4(q)/q arctangent series does not arise from this stationary phase.
For psi(beta)(1-psi(alpha)), differentiation gives psi'(beta)(1-psi(alpha))-psi(beta)psi'(alpha); omitting the second strip-edge term changes the finite identity.

At A=0 the disjoint mask weights the residue by 1-psi(Im z). The accepted Round-24 estimate is for the recombined unmasked physical R1 term and does not separately bound this finite-height filtered share.
The isolated R1 split has the artificial pole A=1/4-u/2-v in the displacement strip. Its residue cancels only against E1, so the recombined radial factor or both split terms must be shifted together.

The logarithmic L1 lemma requires a controlled phase pushforward and integrable uniform discrete BV for the complete actual-profile amplitude; it also holds for the unsigned Dirichlet kernel and by itself proves no transition estimate.
